lines.trans: Hi, Nastya, why are you in a bad mood?
People tore live flowers for pleasure.
Do not be sad, Nastya, everything will be fine.
This is terrible, wicked people act like that.
Let us go somewhere this weekend.
I also wanted to suggest a meeting to you.
Great! What beautiful place shall we go to?
We will go together to the Khimki forest.
And why do we need to go to the forest?
There will be a big rally in defense of the forest.
I thought we would go to the cinema.
Saving living nature is much more important than cinema!
Alright, Nastya, I will gladly go.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: substantivized adjective from выходной день; declines like an adjective

examples.trans: It's a day off, after all.

examples.text: Что ты делаешь в эти выходные?
examples.trans: What are you doing this weekend?
It is the weekend today, everything is cool!

meanings.note: only before a comparative: гораздо хуже

examples.text: Ваня, всё гораздо хуже. Меня обманули.
examples.trans: Vanya, it's much worse than that. I've been cheated.

examples.text: Иди к маме, малыш! Не грусти.
examples.trans: Go to your mama, sweetie! Don't be sad.
Don't be sad, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Привет всем! Что вы тут грустите?
examples.trans: Hello everyone! Why are you sad here?

meanings.note: + infinitive: давай убирать = let's clean up

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: by car, bus, train, in one direction, now

examples.trans: Vitalik, we're going to the Santa Fe.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('living, alive, live').

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
You can't torture a living person like that!

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!
Oh, Samson. What have you come for?
How are we going to build our defence?

examples.text: Вы под нашей защитой. Вам не о чем волноваться.
examples.trans: You are under our protection. You have nothing to worry about.

meanings.note: злая собака = vicious dog; а почему вы такая злая? = why are you so hostile?
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
Then invite me to the movies.
So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.

examples.text: Зачем ты вообще ведёшь её в кино?
examples.trans: Why are you even taking her to the movies?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

examples.text: Куда-нибудь, шеф меня только что уволил.
examples.trans: Anywhere, the chef just fired me.

examples.text: Слушай, а может мы сходим куда-нибудь?
examples.trans: Listen, maybe we should go somewhere?

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки!
examples.trans: Let's drive out to the forest for shashlik!

examples.text: Давайте поедем в лес на шашлыки! Даню вон с собой возьмём.
examples.trans: Let's drive out to the forest for shashlik! We will take Danya here along with us.

examples.text: Смотри, дядя Даня, видишь, побелел! Испугался он зимнего леса.
examples.trans: Look, Uncle Danya has gone pale, see! He is afraid of the winter forest.

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.
There will be a rally tomorrow.

examples.text: Вот так на митингах говори, запомни.
examples.trans: That's how you talk at rallies, remember that.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'строение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'mood, spirits' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood.
I am in a good mood today.

examples.text: С таким настроением, конечно, не будет.
examples.trans: With an attitude like that, of course there won't be.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
used as an exclamation of approval

examples.trans: I know this town really well!

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.
Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Вика, так нельзя поступать со мной!
examples.trans: Vika, you cannot treat me like this!

examples.text: Я всегда стараюсь поступать честно, как он.
examples.trans: I always try to act honestly, like him.

examples.text: Я не понимаю, почему они так поступают.
examples.trans: I do not understand why they act like that.
Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ложить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to offer, to suggest', paired with 'предлагать'.

examples.trans: But you were offered a job.

examples.text: Тебе же предложили работу. Что, плохая работа?
examples.trans: But you were offered a job. What, is it a bad job?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: на природе = out in nature, outdoors

examples.text: Мы давно на природе не были!
examples.trans: We have not been out in nature for a long time!

examples.text: Вот так бы на природе, да? Мы давно на природе не были!
examples.trans: Now if we were out in nature, right? We have not been out in nature for a long time!

examples.text: Вот так бы на природе, да?
examples.trans: Now if we were out in nature, right?
Work, work. It's all for us.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

сорвать.gloss: to disrupt, to ruin; to tear off

meanings.en: to disrupt, to ruin (a lesson or plan)
meanings.note: сорвать урок = to disrupt a class

examples.text: Шум в коридоре чуть не сорвал занятие.
examples.trans: The noise in the corridor almost disrupted the class.

examples.text: Он это сделал в компьютере, в фотошопе. И он урок сорвал!
examples.trans: He made this on the computer, in Photoshop. And he disrupted the lesson!

meanings.en: to save, to rescue from danger
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to save, to rescue', paired with 'спасти'.

examples.text: Все прибежали тебя спасать — и я, и папа!
examples.trans: Everyone came running to save you — both me and Dad!
She is saving you from the hospital!

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over

examples.trans: Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

meanings.note: at the start of a question

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'довольствие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'pleasure' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Даже Лёша начал ходить в садик с удовольствием.
examples.trans: Even Lyosha started going to daycare with pleasure.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жасно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It is terribly cold outside today.

examples.text: Ужасно. Зачем вы мне это рассказываете?
examples.trans: Awful. Why are you telling me this?
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: plural цветы is used for cut flowers / a bouquet
the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
